title: The Handmaid's Tale
summary: The Handmaid's Tale is a futuristic dystopian novel by Canadian author Margaret Atwood published in 1985. It is set in a near-future New England in a patriarchal, totalitarian theonomic state known as the Republic of Gilead, which has overthrown the United States government. Offred is the central character and narrator and one of the "Handmaids": women who are forcibly assigned to produce children for the "Commanders", who are the ruling class in Gilead.

creators.name: Margaret Atwood
creators.lead: Margaret Eleanor Atwood is a Canadian novelist, poet, and literary critic.

pieces.name: Aunt Elizabeth
pieces.sentence: One of the Aunts who works with Aunt Lydia in training the Handmaids.

pieces.name: Aunt Lydia
pieces.sentence: One of the Aunts responsible for indoctrinating and training the Handmaids. She enforces the strict rules and ideologies of Gilead.

pieces.name: Cora

pieces.sentence: A high-ranking official in the Gileadean regime. He is the head of the household where Offred is assigned.

pieces.sentence: A Handmaid who goes through significant emotional and psychological trauma. She is used to showcase the varying degrees of coping mechanisms among Handmaids.

pieces.sentence: Offred’s best friend from before Gilead. Moira is a rebellious and outspoken character who tries to escape the regime multiple times.

pieces.name: Nick
pieces.sentence: The household chauffeur. He becomes Offred’s secret lover and is hinted to be a member of the resistance movement known as Mayday.

pieces.name: Offred
pieces.sentence: The protagonist and narrator of the story. She is a Handmaid assigned to the household of the Commander and Serena Joy. Her real name is never revealed.

pieces.name: Offred's mother

pieces.name: Ofglen
pieces.sentence: Offred’s shopping partner and fellow Handmaid. She is a member of the resistance and tries to recruit Offred.

pieces.name: Professor Pieixoto
pieces.sentence: A scholar from the epilogue who provides historical context to Offred’s narrative.

pieces.name: Rita
pieces.sentence: A Martha in the Commander’s household. She is responsible for cooking and other domestic chores.

pieces.name: Serena Joy
pieces.sentence: The Commander’s wife. Once a televangelist advocating for traditional values, she now resents the Handmaids and her own lack of power within the household.

pieces.name: The Doctor
pieces.sentence: A physician who offers to impregnate Offred, suggesting that many Commanders are sterile.

pieces.name: The Econowives
pieces.sentence: Wives of lower-ranking men who perform all duties (domestic, reproductive, etc.) themselves, without the help of Marthas or Handmaids.

pieces.name: The Eyes
pieces.sentence: Gilead's secret police who spy on the citizens and enforce the regime's rules.

pieces.name: The Guardians
pieces.sentence: Young men who serve as soldiers and police in Gilead, enforcing the regime’s rules.

pieces.name: Boston
pieces.sentence: Nearby Boston is occasionally referenced, and its landmarks and infrastructure are implied to have been overtaken and transformed by the Gileadean regime.
pieces.about: Boston, officially the City of Boston, is the capital and most populous city in the Commonwealth of Massachusetts in the United States. The city serves as the cultural and financial center of the New England region of the Northeastern United States. It has an area of 48.4 sq mi (125 km2) and a population of 675,647 as of the 2020 census, making it the third-largest city in the Northeast after New York City and Philadelphia. The Greater Boston metropolitan statistical area, including and surrounding the city, is the largest in New England and eleventh-largest in the country.

pieces.name: Cambridge, Massachusetts
pieces.sentence: The city of Cambridge, where Harvard University is located, is a significant part of the setting. Gilead’s power structures and the Commander's home are situated in this area.
pieces.about: Cambridge is a city in Middlesex County, Massachusetts, United States. It is a suburb in the Greater Boston metropolitan area, located directly across the Charles River from Boston. The city's population as of the 2020 U.S. census was 118,403, making it the most populous city in the county, the fourth-largest in Massachusetts behind Boston, Worcester, and Springfield, and ninth-most populous in New England. The city was named in honor of the University of Cambridge in Cambridge, England, which was an important center of the Puritan theology that was embraced by the town's founders.

pieces.name: Canada
pieces.sentence: Canada serves as a symbol of hope and freedom for those living under the oppressive regime of Gilead.
pieces.about: Canada is a country in North America. Its ten provinces and three territories extend from the Atlantic Ocean to the Pacific Ocean and northward into the Arctic Ocean, making it the world's second-largest country by total area, with the world's longest coastline. Its border with the United States is the world's longest international land border. The country is characterized by a wide range of both meteorologic and geological regions. It is a sparsely inhabited country of 40 million people, the vast majority residing south of the 55th parallel in urban areas. Canada's capital is Ottawa and its three largest metropolitan areas are Toronto, Montreal, and Vancouver.

pieces.name: Harvard University
pieces.sentence: Many of the buildings and facilities from Harvard University are repurposed by the Gileadean regime. The Wall, where bodies are displayed, is part of Harvard, and the Red Center is located in what used to be a high school in the Harvard area.
pieces.about: Harvard University is a private Ivy League research university in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Founded in 1636 as Harvard College and named for its first benefactor, Puritan clergyman John Harvard, it is the oldest institution of higher learning in the United States. Its influence, wealth, and rankings have made it one of the most prestigious universities in the world.

pieces.name: New England
pieces.sentence: The story is set in the Republic of Gilead, which has overtaken the northeastern United States, including the region of New England.
pieces.about: New England is a region comprising six states in the Northeastern United States: Connecticut, Maine, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Rhode Island, and Vermont. It is bordered by the state of New York to the west and by the Canadian provinces of New Brunswick to the northeast and Quebec to the north. The Gulf of Maine and Atlantic Ocean are to the east and southeast, and Long Island Sound is to the southwest. Boston is New England's largest city and the capital of Massachusetts. Greater Boston is the largest metropolitan area, with nearly a third of New England's population; this area includes Worcester, Massachusetts, the second-largest city in New England, Manchester, New Hampshire, the largest city in New Hampshire, and Providence, Rhode Island, the capital of and largest city in Rhode Island.

pieces.name: Red Center
pieces.sentence: The Red Center is located in what used to be a high school in the Cambridge, Massachusetts area. This location is part of New England, further grounding the fictional setting of Gilead in a real-world context.

pieces.name: Salem, Massachusetts
pieces.sentence: Salem is mentioned in a historical context, known for the Salem witch trials. This reference adds to the theme of religious extremism and persecution in Gilead.
pieces.about: Salem is a historic coastal city in Essex County, Massachusetts, United States, located on the North Shore of Greater Boston. Continuous settlement by Europeans began in 1626 with English colonists. Salem was one of the most significant seaports trading commodities in early American history. Prior to the dissolution of county governments in Massachusetts in 1999, it served as one of two county seats for Essex County, alongside Lawrence.

pieces.name: Bonnet
pieces.sentence: Handmaids wear red dresses and white bonnets, which symbolize their role as fertile women under the control of the regime.
pieces.about: Bonnet has been used as the name for a wide variety of headgear for both sexes—more often female—from the Middle Ages to the present. As with "hat" and "cap", it is impossible to generalize as to the styles for which the word has been used, but there is for both sexes a tendency to use the word for styles in soft material and lacking a brim, or at least one all the way round, rather than just at the front. Yet the term has also been used, for example, for steel helmets. This was from Scotland, where the term has long been especially popular.

pieces.name: Red dress

pieces.name: Scrabble
pieces.sentence: The Scrabble board symbolizes the small freedoms and clandestine activities the Commander allows Offred during their private meetings.
pieces.about: Scrabble is a word game in which two to four players score points by placing tiles, each bearing a single letter, onto a game board divided into a 15×15 grid of squares. The tiles must form words that, in crossword fashion, read left to right in rows or downward in columns and are included in a standard dictionary or lexicon.

pieces.name: Veil
pieces.sentence: A symbol of the Handmaids' subservience and removal from society's norms.
pieces.about: A veil is an article of clothing or hanging cloth that is intended to cover some part of the head or face, or an object of some significance. Veiling has a long history in European, Asian, and African societies. The practice has been prominent in different forms in Judaism, Christianity, and Islam. The practice of veiling is especially associated with women and sacred objects, though in some cultures, it is men, rather than women, who are expected to wear a veil. Besides its enduring religious significance, veiling continues to play a role in some modern secular contexts, such as wedding customs.

pieces.name: Dystopian Society

pieces.name: Fertility
pieces.about: Fertility is the ability to have babies or to reproduce. When fertility rates in a community increase, more babies are born. Fertility is the quality of a human's ability to produce offspring, which is dependent on age, health, and other factors.

pieces.about: The power or right to act, speak, or think as one wants without hindrance or restraint.

pieces.about: A strict adherence to traditional beliefs, values, or doctrines, often within a religious or ideological context. It typically involves a literal interpretation of sacred texts or principles and a resistance to change or modernization. Fundamentalist movements can be found in various religions and ideologies, and they often advocate for a return to what they perceive as the fundamental or original principles of their faith or ideology. pieces.name: Women's Rights
pieces.sentence: The story delves into the control of women's bodies and reproductive functions, emphasizing the reduction of women to their biological roles.
pieces.about: Women's rights refer to the entitlements and freedoms that are inherently due to women as human beings, ensuring their equality and dignity in all aspects of life. These rights encompass various areas, including legal, social, economic, and political spheres. Ensuring women's rights is essential for achieving gender equality, promoting social justice, and building inclusive and equitable societies.

pieces.name: Control
pieces.sentence: Gilead's regime employs various forms of repression and control to maintain social order, including surveillance, propaganda, and indoctrination.
pieces.about: Control is a multifaceted concept that plays a crucial role in various aspects of life, from personal self-regulation to organizational management and technological systems. Effective control mechanisms enhance efficiency, safety, and well-being, while ethical considerations ensure that control is exercised responsibly and equitably. Understanding and balancing control across different contexts helps in achieving desired outcomes while promoting autonomy, fairness, and mutual respect.

pieces.about: An imagined society where people live under harsh control, often presented as ideal, used to warn where the present could lead.

pieces.name: Gender and Women's Rights
pieces.sentence: At the heart of the novel is the exploration of gender dynamics and power struggles, where women are subjugated and controlled by men in positions of authority.
pieces.about: Women's rights focus on the struggle for gender equality and the fight against discrimination and oppression faced by women. It encompasses issues such as access to education, equal employment opportunities, reproductive rights, freedom from violence, and the right to political participation. This theme highlights the social, cultural, and legal barriers that women encounter and emphasizes the importance of empowerment, advocacy, and reform in achieving gender equality. Literature addressing women's rights often explores personal and collective stories of resistance, resilience, and the ongoing quest for justice and equality for women around the world.

pieces.about: Dr. Jekyll's struggle with identity is a key theme. The transformation into Hyde challenges traditional notions of selfhood, prompting reflections on the stability and consistency of one's identity.

pieces.name: Environmental Planner
pieces.sentence: Manages and mitigates the environmental impacts of the regime's policies and practices, including waste management and resource allocation.
pieces.about:
An environmental planner is a professional who specializes in assessing, managing, and promoting sustainable development practices that minimize environmental impact and enhance quality of life for communities. Environmental planners work at the intersection of urban planning, environmental science, and public policy to address environmental challenges and promote resilience and sustainability.

Key aspects of being an environmental planner include:

Environmental Assessment: Environmental planners conduct assessments of natural resources, ecosystems, land use, and environmental conditions to identify potential impacts of proposed development projects or policies. They analyze data, conduct field studies, and evaluate potential risks to ecosystems, wildlife, water resources, and air quality.
Land Use Planning: Environmental planners collaborate with urban planners, government agencies, developers, and community stakeholders to develop land use plans and zoning regulations that balance development needs with environmental conservation goals. They aim to minimize urban sprawl, protect sensitive habitats, and promote sustainable land use practices.
Policy Development: Environmental planners contribute to the development of environmental policies, regulations, and guidelines at local, regional, and national levels. They advocate for policies that promote environmental protection, resource conservation, climate resilience, and sustainable development practices.
Community Engagement: Environmental planners engage with local communities, stakeholders, and interest groups to gather input, build consensus, and promote public participation in decision-making processes related to environmental planning initiatives. They facilitate public meetings, workshops, and outreach campaigns to raise awareness and solicit feedback on environmental issues and proposed projects.
Sustainability Planning: Environmental planners integrate principles of sustainability into planning processes and decision-making, considering economic, social, and environmental factors in project design and implementation. They promote strategies such as green infrastructure, energy efficiency, waste reduction, and sustainable transportation to create more resilient and livable communities.
Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA): Environmental planners conduct EIAs to evaluate the potential environmental, social, and economic impacts of proposed development projects. They assess factors such as air and water quality, biodiversity, noise pollution, and cultural heritage to inform project decision-making and mitigate adverse impacts.

Environmental planners work in various settings, including government agencies, consulting firms, non-profit organizations, and research institutions. They collaborate with multidisciplinary teams of professionals, including urban planners, engineers, ecologists, economists, and policymakers, to address complex environmental challenges and promote sustainable development practices.

pieces.about: A judge is a person who presides over court proceedings, either alone or as a part of a panel of judges. In an adversarial system the judge hears all the witnesses and any other evidence presented by the barristers or solicitors of the case, assesses the credibility and arguments of the parties, and then issues a ruling in the case based on their interpretation of the law and their own personal judgment. A judge is expected to conduct the trial impartially and, typically, in an open court.

pieces.name: Theologian
pieces.sentence: Interprets religious texts and doctrines to justify and reinforce the regime's authority and policies, providing theological justification for societal norms.
pieces.about: Theology is the study of religious belief from a religious perspective. More narrowly it is the study of the nature of the divine. It is taught as an academic discipline, typically in universities and seminaries. It occupies itself with the unique content of analyzing the supernatural, but also deals with religious epistemology, asks and seeks to answer the question of revelation. Revelation pertains to the acceptance of God, gods, or deities, as not only transcendent or above the natural world, but also willing and able to interact with the natural world and to reveal themselves to humankind.

pieces.name: Therapist

pieces.about: A therapist is a licensed mental health professional who provides counseling and support to individuals, couples, families, and groups to help them manage and overcome mental health issues, emotional challenges, and behavioral problems. Therapists work in various settings, including private practices, hospitals, schools, and community centers. Their goal is to help clients develop coping strategies, improve their well-being, and achieve personal growth.

pieces.about: A doctor, also known as a physician, is a medical professional who is trained to diagnose and treat illnesses, injuries, and other health conditions. Doctors play a crucial role in maintaining public health, providing care and advice to patients, and advancing medical knowledge through research. Doctors are vital to the healthcare system, dedicated to diagnosing, treating, and preventing illnesses to improve patient health and well-being. The path to becoming a doctor is rigorous, requiring extensive education and training, but the profession is highly rewarding, offering the opportunity to make a significant impact on people's lives. As medical science and technology continue to evolve, the role of doctors will also adapt, ensuring that they remain at the forefront of providing high-quality healthcare.
